cards.explanation: The answer is back to every town where they preached. Paul, the traveling teacher, tells Barnabas, his partner in the work, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.” That's a check-in tour. I think Paul wanted to see the faces behind the word he'd preached. (Acts 15:36)

The answer is that Mark deserted them in Pamphylia. The text gives that reason, friends. It says Paul thought it best not to take Mark, John also called Mark, “…because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.” That's the writer telling us why. I think it was a hard thing for both men to sit across from. (Acts 15:38)

The answer is False. They don't settle it and keep traveling together. The text says, “Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company.” No compromise and no coin flip is mentioned. I think that one stings, because they'd done so much together. (Acts 15:39)

The answer is Cyprus. “Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus…” Barnabas wanted to take Mark, and this verse shows him doing it, friends. Paul went a different direction, since they parted company. (Acts 15:37, 39)

The answer is strengthening. Paul “…traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.” He's building people up, and Silas, the one Paul chose, is with him. That's a good way to spend a road trip, bakers. (Acts 15:40-41)

The answer is True. Timothy, a disciple Paul found in Lystra, had a good name. “The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.” Two towns spoke well of him, friends, and I'd love to get that review on my cookies. (Acts 16:2)

The answer is False. Paul does not leave Timothy behind. “Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him…” Paul found a disciple the brothers spoke well of and brought him along. I think Timothy had a lot of road ahead of him. (Acts 16:2-3)

The answer is that the Jews there knew his father was Greek. Paul circumcised Timothy “…on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.” Timothy's mother was a believing Jewish woman, and his father was Greek. That is the reason the text gives, friends. (Acts 16:1, 3)

The answer is that they grow in numbers every day. “So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.” Strong in faith, bigger in numbers, and it kept going day after day. That's a full cookie jar, bakers. (Acts 16:5)

The answer is False. The Spirit of Jesus does not let them in. They tried to enter Bithynia, “…but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.” It's the second no in a row, friends, since the Holy Spirit had already kept them from speaking the word in Asia. So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas. (Acts 16:6-8)

The answer is Macedonia. The text says, “During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him…” I think a plea like that gets your attention faster than a smoking oven. His words are “Come over to Macedonia and help us.” (Acts 16:9)
The answer is to come over and help them. The man says, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.” It's a short plea and a clear one, friends. (Acts 16:9)

The answer is True. “As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia…” There's no long delay in the text, and they get ready right then. Nobody hits snooze, friends. (Acts 16:10)

The answer is that God has called them to preach there. As soon as Paul had seen the vision, they got ready to leave for Macedonia, “…concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.” They concluded it was God's call, bakers. The text says it plainly. (Acts 16:9-10)
